parsed.explanation: Thin-data small-island jurisdiction. The dominant exposure: a live, court-affirmed (Feb 2024) criminalisation of same-sex conduct (up to 10 years) in a state with no SOGI protections, no LGBT civil-society infrastructure, and documented bias violence — the statute is not a dead letter and the record shows it reaching a trans person directly: a cross-dressing teenager assaulted and then charged with 'fraud for pretending to be a woman' (2019), i.e. presentation itself prosecuted as deception, though the charge was withdrawn. No entry/screening restrictions or facility rules are documented, and the head of government condemned a transphobic attack (mild mitigation), but incidents are dated individual cases, enforcement frequency is unknown, and recourse is effectively nil. This sits below the tolerant-society-with-dead-letter-law tier (0.55–0.65) because the law was just judicially upheld and has been wielded against gender presentation; societal hostility is documented with no remedy, and an outed trans visitor with a partner faces the full criminal exposure. Extrapolating from live criminalisation, thin rule-of-law recourse, and no protective infrastructure resolves around the elevated/high-risk boundary: 0.45.
